statement: PackOptions has exactly three fields: source_retries (fresh-handle retries after first capture attempt), include_index, and CompressionProfile. Defaults are source_retries=2, include_index=true, profile=Balanced.
evidence_in_source: code; used by tests/filesystem_workflow.rs and tests/cdc_dedup.rs via PackOptions::default()

statement: Default source_retries=2 (three capture attempts before SourceUnstable) is a numeric parameter chosen without cited measurement of mutation rates or retry success on live trees.
research_needed: Measure capture success versus retry count on actively-written trees (logs, databases, build dirs) across platforms.
decision_needed: Is 2 retries the right default, and should it be user-configurable in the CLI?

statement: ExtractionReport exposes entries_created, logical_bytes_written, confinement (ConfinementMode), and metadata_not_restored as a Vec of free-text strings.

Extraction fidelity loss is reported only as human-readable strings ('path: reason'); there are no structured per-entry reason codes, metadata class identifiers, or a FidelityReport-shaped extraction record.
research_needed: Usability study of extraction loss reports; define a machine-readable schema aligned with FidelityReport classes.
decision_needed: What structured, versioned form must the extraction-side restoration report take for v1?

statement: pack_directory builds a validated EAM from a local directory and encodes it as INDEXED via ecf::encode with WriteOptions{include_index}.
pack_directory_stream writes the same EAM as STREAM to any never-seeked Write sink (pipe/stdout); doc states LAI, PCR and AUX equal the INDEXED encoding and only PCI differs.

pack_directory_stream has no test or CLI caller (CLI stream pack uses plan_directory + encode_stream at entrybound-cli/src/lib.rs:760-780); its identity-equivalence claim is untested for this entry point.
evidence_in_source: grep: no references outside archive.rs re-export
research_needed: Add a test packing one tree with pack_directory and pack_directory_stream and asserting equal LAI/PCR/AUX and different PCI.

statement: plan_directory scans and plans a directory, returning the EAM without encoding, so callers choose or create output only after planning succeeds and never leave a partial artifact.
evidence_in_source: doc comment; used by entrybound-cli/src/lib.rs:760 and tests/random_access.rs::planned_fixture

statement: plan_directory_encrypted (crate-private) runs the same scan but chunks with an EncryptedBoundaryKey and a caller-supplied chunker_id prefix; called from crypto/mod.rs:419.

replan_archive_encrypted rebuilds only the encrypted physical plan from an authenticated EAM: entries, metadata, FidelityReport and plaintext stay authoritative while key-derived boundaries and all physical plans are regenerated for a fresh encryption epoch.
evidence_in_source: doc comment; called by crypto/container.rs:885-896 rotate_encryption_epoch; tests/crypto_v1.rs::password_change_rotates_the_key_and_invalidates_the_old_password

statement: replan_archive rebuilds the native physical plan purely from verified logical objects (no host filesystem), discarding transform plans, dictionaries, chunk groups, reconstruction data/regions/fallbacks/audits and Index before running plan_archive_v6.

Replan reassembles each ContentObject, rejects plaintext whose SHA-256 differs from its digest (Corrupt/ContentDigestMismatch), rejects rechunking that changes the logical digest, and rejects distinct plaintext under one chunk ID (ChunkIdentityCollision).

chunker_id inconsistency: replan_archive records 'entrybound/gear-cdc-v1/min-*/target-*/max-*' while fresh packs record the frozen 'gear-norm-v1/min-*...' IDs (chunker.rs:79-108). PCR hashes chunker_id (identity.rs:538-560), so identical chunking yields a different PCR.
refines_or_supersedes: diverges from chunker.rs:80-108 frozen gear-norm-v1 identifiers
evidence_in_source: code comparison across filesystem.rs, chunker.rs, identity.rs
research_needed: Test that Replan(Balanced) of a Balanced pack gives the same PCR as the original; fix or document the second identifier.
decision_needed: Which chunker_id string is canonical for replanned archives, and is 'gear-cdc-v1' a registered identifier?

statement: replan_archive_encrypted and replan_archive are near-duplicate ~120-line bodies differing only in parameter selection/chunking function and chunker_id prefix; the divergent chunker_id arises in this duplication.

Replan resets descriptor features (keeping only conversion/preservation/metadata bits), layout=Indexed, role=Complete, budget_declared=true, stream_dedup_window=0, default budget/decode, planner_id from profile, zeroed LAI/PCR/AUX and PCI=None.

Replan clones the source descriptor, so format_major/minor, format_namespace, identity_profile and digest_algorithm are inherited; whether repack migrates older archives to current format or identity profile versions is undefined here.
decision_needed: Should repack/replan upgrade descriptors to the current format version and identity profile, or preserve them?

statement: CDC parameter selection is archive-wide: one ChunkingParameters set is chosen for all files by select_parameters over every plaintext from profile.chunking_candidates (lowest estimated cost, earlier candidate wins ties).
Replan materializes every ContentObject plaintext in memory simultaneously (Vec of boxed plaintexts plus chunk copies); bounded-memory or beyond-RAM repack is not implemented.
research_needed: Measure peak RSS of repack versus archive logical size; design spill/streaming replan.
decision_needed: Must v1 repack operate within a declared memory bound for archives larger than RAM?

statement: Pack root checks: uninspectable path -> PolicyRefused/InputNotDirectory; root symlink -> Unsupported/UnsupportedEntryKind; non-directory -> InputNotDirectory; Windows root with FILE_ATTRIBUTE_REPARSE_POINT (0x400) -> Unsupported/InvalidReparsePoint.

On Windows any source object with the reparse attribute (symlinks, junctions, cloud placeholders, dedup stubs) aborts the entire pack with Unsupported/InvalidReparsePoint, citing lack of an audited safe API for exact tag/payload capture.
research_needed: Survey reparse-tag prevalence on real Windows trees (OneDrive, WSL, dedup); assess safe-Rust APIs (windows-rs) for FSCTL_GET_REPARSE_POINT under unsafe_code=forbid.
decision_needed: Should v1 capture reparse data, skip with a declared loss, or refuse, and may unsafe platform FFI be admitted?

statement: Windows scan checks the reparse attribute before is_symlink, so Windows symlinks are always refused; the non-unix UTF-8 link_target_from_os path is effectively unreachable during Windows pack.
Source traversal holds a cap-std Dir opened with ambient authority at the root and descends through DirEntry::open_dir handles, recursion carrying logical ancestor components.

CLI defaults: pack output is the input's final name plus '.eb' in the CWD (fallback 'archive.eb'); unpack destination strips any extension beside the archive, or appends '.unpacked' when none (e.g., 'backup.tar' -> 'backup').

Materialization draws plaintext only through the ChunkSource trait: INDEXED uses chunks retained in the opened model, STREAM uses bounded StagedChunks. Extraction never reads unverified archive bytes.
unpack fully opens and verifies the INDEXED archive with open_with_limits(policy.budget, policy.decode) before creating anything, then clones the full chunk plaintext map for materialization.
INDEXED extraction holds all chunk plaintext in memory and then clones it; bounded-memory, incremental or per-entry INDEXED extraction is not implemented in this path.
research_needed: Measure peak memory of unpack versus archive size; compare with STREAM staged extraction.
decision_needed: Must INDEXED extraction honour a memory bound independent of archive size in v1?

statement: unpack_opened materializes an already authenticated and verified OpenedArchive; crypto callers use it only after recipient unlock and envelope/segment authentication, so a failed credential never creates destination objects.
evidence_in_source: doc comment; used at entrybound-cli/src/lib.rs:2355; entrybound-cli/tests/crypto_cli.rs::hybrid_pack_public_inspect_verify_and_unpack (L31-137, tampered archive leaves no destination). tests/crypto_v1.rs::password_archive_unlocks_and_wrong_password_does_not_materialize never calls an extraction API, so it does not exercise this path
research_needed: Add a library-level test calling unpack_opened after open_encrypted, and a negative test showing that failed authentication creates no destination.

statement: unpack_stream completes the sequential pass with staged content first; nothing is created until framing, every chunk digest, EAM invariants, identity roots, footer binding and exact length are established; staging is released on failure. Policy budget/decode override supplied limits.

Only collision refusal exists: CollisionPolicy has a single Refuse variant and materialize rejects anything else ('bootstrap extractor supports only collision refusal'). Overwrite, skip, rename and newer-wins modes are absent.
decision_needed: Which collision modes (overwrite, skip, keep-newer) does v1 need, and with what safety defaults?

statement: Before creating the destination root, every Symlink entry is checked against SymlinkPolicy and any ReparsePoint entry is refused, so these policy failures leave no destination.

Reparse-point extraction is refused under every ReparsePolicy: Refuse by policy, KnownSafe because no opaque tag is recognized as KnownSafe, All because 'no audited safe API in this build'. Any reparse entry aborts the whole extraction.
decision_needed: Which reparse tags qualify as KnownSafe, and should unsupported reparse entries be skipped-with-report instead of aborting?

statement: Destination root is created with non-recursive std::fs::create_dir; an existing directory is accepted and extraction merges into it; an existing non-directory is ExtractionCollision; failure to hold the root is ExtractionContainmentUnavailable.

The destination root is resolved through the ambient path and is_dir()/open_ambient_dir follow symlinks, so a root that is a symlink to a directory is followed; the trust boundary for the root path itself is unspecified.
research_needed: Adversarial test with destination root replaced by a symlink between create_dir and open.
decision_needed: Must the extraction root be required to be a real (non-symlink) directory?

statement: ExtractionReport.confinement is hardcoded KernelEnforced and WeakerReported is never produced, although cap-std may resolve paths in userspace on platforms lacking openat2/RESOLVE_BENEATH (Windows, macOS, older Linux).
research_needed: Determine cap-std's resolution mechanism per OS/kernel; race tests swapping directories for symlinks during extraction; report the achieved mode honestly.
decision_needed: How is achieved confinement detected and reported per platform?

statement: Extraction passes: (1) directories and hardlink representative files in entry order; (2) remaining hardlink aliases; (3) directory metadata in reverse entry order; (4) symlinks last, so no extraction write traverses an extracted symlink.
Directory metadata (including mtime) is applied before symlinks are created, so creating symlinks afterwards alters the parent directories' mtimes. This loss is not recorded in metadata_not_restored.
research_needed: Round-trip test asserting directory mtimes for directories containing symlinks; reorder or re-apply directory times after symlink creation.

statement: Files are created with create_new(true) and directories with create_dir, both atomic no-replace; ensure_absent pre-checks with no-follow symlink_metadata; existing objects map to PolicyRefused/ExtractionCollision.

Extraction is not transactional: a mid-extraction failure (collision, I/O, non-UTF-8 component, hardlink failure) leaves created objects in place with no rollback. The partial-failure test asserts an earlier file remains.
research_needed: Evaluate stage-then-rename extraction cost and cross-platform atomicity.
decision_needed: Should v1 extraction stage into a temporary sibling and publish atomically, or document partial output?

statement: logical_bytes_written counts only representative regular files (hardlink aliases and symlinks excluded); entries_created counts directories, files, aliases and symlinks; overflow yields ResourceLimit.
Hardlink aliases are created with Dir::hard_link from the first path of the group. Any failure aborts extraction with an Io diagnostic, and there is no copy fallback.
On destinations without hardlink support (FAT/exFAT, some network or cloud filesystems), archives with hardlink groups cannot be extracted at all because no copy-fallback policy exists.
research_needed: Test extraction of hardlink groups onto exFAT/SMB/FUSE targets.
decision_needed: Should hardlink restoration fall back to independent copies with a declared loss?

statement: With SparsePolicy::Restore and a SparseMap, the writer set_len()s to logical size and seeks to write only declared data-extent bytes; otherwise it writes all chunk plaintext sequentially. Holes are assumed zero, relying on EAM validation (eam/validate.rs:876-920).
The sparse Restore write path runs on non-unix too without setting a platform sparse attribute (no FSCTL_SET_SPARSE); on non-unix the report says sparse topology restoration is unavailable.

Pack is not streaming or bounded-memory: every entry and full file plaintext (read_to_end) is accumulated in memory before chunking and planning. Capture of trees larger than RAM, or from unseekable sources, is not implemented.
research_needed: Measure peak RSS versus tree size; design spill-to-disk or incremental chunking that preserves determinism.
decision_needed: What memory bound must v1 pack honour, and is whole-tree archive-wide CDC selection compatible with streaming capture?

statement: Pack-time metadata accounting sums symlink target bytes, xattr name+value bytes, ACL xattr bytes, sparse maps (16 per extent + 8) and 16 macOS bytes against bootstrap_resource_policy().max_metadata_bytes (1 GiB); exceeding it gives ResourceLimit.

PackOptions accepts no caller resource budget; the pack-time metadata limit is hardwired to the bootstrap policy despite the message 'caller bootstrap metadata policy', and entry count, total bytes and path depth are not bounded during scan.
decision_needed: Should pack accept a caller ResourceBudget and enforce it incrementally during scan?

statement: Scan::finish merges the static per-platform bootstrap FidelityReport with classes observed unavailable during capture (reason 'did not provide a reliable no-follow value'), sorted and deduplicated by class.
Filesystem-capture FidelityIssues are always archive-wide (entry_scope None). A metadata class lost for a few entries, e.g. EACCES reading one ACL, is not attributed to those entries.
decision_needed: Must FidelityReport identify which entries lost which metadata class?

statement: The captured class list is static per platform while unavailable classes are added dynamically, so on Linux 'security.acls' or 'posix.xattrs' can appear as both captured and unavailable in one FidelityReport.
decision_needed: What are the normative semantics when a class is captured for some entries and unavailable for others?

statement: finish_with performs exact archive-wide dedup: ContentObjects keyed by logical digest and Chunks by chunk ID; a divergent object for the same digest is Corrupt/ContentDigestMismatch; divergent chunk bytes for one ID is ChunkIdentityCollision.

New filesystem archives get a descriptor with format 0.1, namespace 'ecf/bootstrap-v1', layout Indexed, role Complete, budget_declared true, identity profile IdentityV1, SHA-256, a v6 planner_id, and the selected chunker_id ('{prefix}/min/target/max' when encrypted).
evidence_in_source: code; tests/filesystem_workflow.rs asserts planner_id 'balanced-v6' and chunker_id 'gear-norm-v1/min-131072/target-524288/max-2097152'

statement: Writers still emit format version 0.1 in namespace 'ecf/bootstrap-v1'; the transition to a frozen v1 format version and namespace, and the compatibility promise for bootstrap-namespace archives, is undecided.
decision_needed: When and how does the writer move from ecf/bootstrap-v1 0.1 to a frozen v1, and must v1 readers accept bootstrap archives?

statement: Before planning, physical_order is the sorted chunk-digest order and plans, dictionaries, groups and reconstruction maps are empty; plan_archive_v6 then assigns plans and physical layout.

Hardlink groups are formed from ≥2 captured paths sharing (dev, ino); members must agree on content digest and full MetadataSet, else PolicyRefused/SourceUnstable; group ID = hardlink_group_id(content, paths), attached as posix.hardlink-group metadata.

Files with nlink>1 whose other links lie outside the packed tree (single member captured) receive no hardlink group and no fidelity note; aliases are read and captured separately and deduplicated by content digest.

plan_observed_archive (crate-private) plans adapter-reconciled entries and plaintexts through the native v6 pipeline with unencrypted CDC, always sets FEATURE_CONVERSION_PROVENANCE_V1 (bit 13), sets LEGACY_PRESERVATION_V1 (bit 14) with preservation evidence, and applies native identities.
evidence_in_source: doc comment; callers legacy/zip.rs:897, legacy/tar.rs:828, legacy/sevenz.rs:2037, legacy/import.rs:367; tooling.rs unit tests

statement: Adapter boundary: legacy adapters use the native pipeline only after resolving foreign evidence into valid EAM entries; ZIP compression and ZIP structure never cross into native planning.
Metadata feature bits: any entry using platform-security metadata v1 sets FEATURE_POSIX_METADATA_V1|FEATURE_PLATFORM_SECURITY_METADATA_V1 (bits 15,16); otherwise any POSIX v1 usage sets bit 15.

Every Windows-packed entry records windows.file-attributes and windows.creation-time, so every Windows archive requires incompatible feature bits 15 and 16. Readers lacking platform-security support cannot open any Windows-created archive.
decision_needed: Should portable Windows metadata be a compat or read-only-compat feature, rather than incompat, so minimal readers can extract content?

statement: Deterministic enumeration: each directory's entries are sorted by file name (OsString order) before capture, so creation order does not affect entry order, CDC or planning.
evidence_in_source: code; tests/filesystem_workflow.rs::filesystem_creation_order_cannot_change_cdc_output (asserts LAI and PCR equal; PCI may differ via Windows creation-time AUX)

statement: Non-UTF-8 source file names are refused (Unsupported/InvalidPathComponent) and abort the entire pack; LogicalPath is built only via from_utf8, so POSIX byte-string names are not capturable.
research_needed: Measure prevalence of non-UTF-8 names in real Linux trees and legacy archives; compare with tar/pax behaviour.
decision_needed: Should the filesystem adapter capture byte-string names (PathEncoding bytes) or skip-and-report?

statement: Unix symlink capture uses no-follow symlink_metadata and read_link_contents, storing exact target bytes (possibly non-UTF-8) via LinkTarget::canonical, plus xattrs and macOS metadata, with a before/after stability check.

Directory capture compares handle metadata before and after metadata capture, and again after recursing into children, so on Unix a directory changed during the scan (via mtime/ctime/nlink) fails with SourceUnstable.
Special files (FIFOs, sockets, block and character devices) abort pack with Unsupported/UnsupportedEntryKind; EntryKind has only Directory, File, Symlink and ReparsePoint.
refines_or_supersedes: narrows spec §3.3 seven-variant EntryKind (Fifo, Socket, BlockDevice, CharDevice absent)
decision_needed: Are special-file EntryKinds in v1 scope or a declared non-goal?

statement: FidelityReport declares 'special-files' unavailable ('not captured'), yet the scanner refuses the whole pack on meeting one, so no archive containing that loss can exist. No omit-and-report mode is implemented.
decision_needed: Should unsupported source objects be omitted with an entry-scoped declared loss or refuse the pack (possibly policy-selected)?

statement: File capture opens a fresh handle per attempt, requires a regular file, reads the whole file, and accepts it only if before/after metadata match and byte count equals final length; after retries+1 attempts it fails PolicyRefused/SourceUnstable.
Any unstable source file or directory aborts the entire pack; there is no skip, warn, snapshot (VSS, btrfs/ZFS) or best-effort mode for live trees.
decision_needed: What pack behaviour is required for actively-changing sources (abort, skip-with-report, snapshot integration)?

statement: Unix source-stability predicate compares dev, ino, mode, nlink, uid, gid, size, mtime seconds+ns, and ctime seconds+ns.

The non-unix (Windows) stability predicate compares only length, modification time and executable (always false). File ID, change time and attributes are ignored, so same-size rewrites that preserve mtime go undetected during capture.
research_needed: Race tests on NTFS rewriting files with preserved mtime during pack; consider ChangeTime/file index via safe APIs.

statement: ACLs, xattrs, sparse extents and macOS metadata are captured through ambient path strings (root joined with components) or a second open, not the held handle; the stability check covers handle metadata only, so a concurrent swap could attach another object's metadata.
research_needed: Adversarial rename/swap tests during pack; fd-based xattr/ACL capture feasibility in safe Rust.

statement: Captured MetadataSet per entry: core.executable and core.mtime always; Unix adds posix.mode (masked 0o7777), numeric uid and gid; plus xattrs, sparse map, non-empty ACLs, macOS items, and Windows attributes/creation time where available.
Ownership is captured only as numeric uid/gid. User/group names and Windows owner or group SIDs are not captured, so ownership cannot be remapped by name on another host.
decision_needed: Must v1 capture owner/group names (tar uname/gname parity) or SIDs?

statement: Windows capture masks out DIRECTORY (0x10), SPARSE_FILE (0x200) and REPARSE_POINT (0x400) as 'semantic authority bits', and converts creation FILETIME to Unix seconds with Hectonanosecond precision (out of range gives InvalidWindowsMetadata).

macOS capture records st_flags and birthtime (Nanosecond precision, restorable=false) via ambient no-follow symlink_metadata; invalid nanoseconds give InvalidMacosMetadata; 16 metadata bytes are accounted.
macOS-specific capture (flags, birthtime) and its FidelityReport classes have no unit or integration test; in-file tests are gated to linux/unix/windows only.
research_needed: Add macOS CI round-trip tests for flags, birthtime and com.apple.* xattrs (resource fork, FinderInfo).

statement: Linux ACL capture reads system.posix_acl_access (and _default for directories) xattrs. errno 1/13/45/61/95 marks archive-wide 'security.acls' unavailable and drops that entry's ACLs; other errors abort pack with Io.

ACL capture is unimplemented on all non-Linux platforms (macOS extended ACLs, Windows DACL/SACL, FreeBSD NFSv4): 'security.acls' is reported unavailable because there is 'no audited safe exact ACL capture adapter'.
research_needed: Assess safe-Rust ACL APIs for macOS/Windows/FreeBSD under unsafe_code=forbid.
decision_needed: Which non-Linux ACL dialects are v1 capture targets?

statement: Linux POSIX ACL xattr codec: version-2 header plus 8-byte entries; validates tag/qualifier pairs (USER_OBJ, USER, GROUP_OBJ, GROUP, MASK, OTHER) and rwx-only permissions (else Nonconforming/InvalidAcl); decodes to Posix1e Allow entries and re-encodes symmetrically.
The canonical ACL permission bits differ from Linux bit order: write stays 0x2, Linux read (0x4) maps to canonical 0x1, and Linux execute (0x1) maps to canonical 0x4.
research_needed: Confirm the canonical ACL permission registry in the specification matches this mapping (and NFSv4 mask ordering).

statement: Unix xattr capture lists all names except the POSIX ACL xattrs (all namespaces including trusted.*, security.*, com.apple.*) with no filtering. It is bounded at 4096 xattrs per entry (ResourceLimit); an xattr vanishing mid-read is SourceUnstable; errno 1/13/45/61/95 marks 'posix.xattrs' unavailable.
The per-entry bound of 4096 xattrs is described as a 'per-entry format bound' but is a code literal with no cited measurement or specification reference in this slice.
research_needed: Cross-check with the format specification and measure maximum xattr counts in real trees (SELinux, macOS quarantine, Samba).

statement: On non-unix, xattr capture always reports 'posix.xattrs' unavailable. NTFS alternate data streams and extended attributes are never captured and are not listed as an unavailable class.
research_needed: Survey ADS prevalence (Zone.Identifier, macOS-origin streams) and Windows EA usage; feasibility of safe capture.
decision_needed: Must NTFS ADS be captured or explicitly declared as lost in FidelityReport for v1?

statement: FidelityReport completeness gap: classes the scanner never captures are absent from the unavailable list, including atime, ctime, Linux birthtime (statx), NTFS ADS, Linux inode flags (chattr) and owner names. Declared-loss completeness is unverified.
research_needed: Enumerate all source-observable metadata per platform and diff against captured+unavailable classes.
decision_needed: Must FidelityReport enumerate every known uncaptured class for the source platform?

statement: Linux sparse capture reopens the file and walks SEEK_DATA/SEEK_HOLE. EINVAL/ENOTSUP marks 'posix.sparse-map' unavailable; a non-progressing extent is SourceUnstable. A SparseMap is recorded for every probed regular file, including fully dense ones.
evidence_in_source: code; unix round-trip test (256 KiB file with data at 128 KiB)

statement: Sparse maps come from filesystem allocation state, so identical logical trees on different filesystems or after copying may yield different posix.sparse-map metadata and AUX roots. Cross-filesystem AUX determinism is unmeasured.
research_needed: Pack the same tree on ext4/xfs/btrfs/tmpfs/zfs, after cp and cp --sparse=always, and compare AUX roots.
decision_needed: Should sparse maps be recorded only when holes exist, or be excluded from AUX?

statement: Because nearly every Linux-captured file carries a sparse map, the default SparsePolicy::Logical adds a 'materialized as logical bytes' note for almost every file, flooding metadata_not_restored with non-losses.
research_needed: Extract a typical Linux-packed tree with default policy and count report lines.
decision_needed: Should only files with real holes produce sparse restoration notes?

statement: Sparse capture is unimplemented on macOS, Windows and BSDs: 'posix.sparse-map' is reported unavailable ('reliable SEEK_DATA/SEEK_HOLE capture is unavailable on this platform').
Hardlink detection is unimplemented on non-unix (Windows): hardlink_identity returns None, and the report lists 'posix ownership/mode/hardlinks' as unavailable.
core.executable on Unix is true if any of the 0o111 bits is set; on non-unix it is always false and 'core.executable' is reported unavailable.

Timestamp capture handles pre-epoch times (negative seconds with positive nanosecond normalization), overflow gives ResourceLimit, precision is Hectonanosecond on Windows and Nanosecond elsewhere, and mtime is marked restorable.
Only modification time is captured as core time; access time, status change time and Linux birthtime are neither captured nor declared unavailable.
decision_needed: Which timestamps beyond mtime are v1 capture targets or declared losses?

statement: Declared captured classes: core.mtime and symlink-target always; Unix adds core.executable, posix.mode/uid/gid/hardlink-group/xattrs; Linux adds posix.sparse-map and security.acls; Windows adds windows.file-attributes/creation-time; macOS adds macos.flags/birthtime.
Windows security descriptors (owner, DACL, SACL) and exact opaque reparse payloads are never captured; both are declared unavailable because 'no audited safe wrapper' exposes the bytes.
research_needed: Evaluate safe crates for GetFileSecurity/BackupRead and FSCTL_GET_REPARSE_POINT; threat-model restoring SDs.
decision_needed: Is Windows security-descriptor capture v1 scope, and may an audited unsafe FFI boundary be admitted?

statement: FidelityReport.filesystem is always empty (filesystem type is never detected) and degraded is always empty in filesystem capture; only platform (std::env::consts::OS) is filled.
Destination paths are resolved component by component with cap-std Dir::open_dir from a cloned root handle; any failure is PolicyRefused/ExtractionContainmentUnavailable.

Extraction requires UTF-8 LogicalPath components ('bootstrap extraction requires UTF-8 path components'). The check runs per entry during materialization, so a byte-encoded path fails mid-extraction after earlier entries exist.
decision_needed: Should non-UTF-8 components be pre-checked before destination creation, or restored as native bytes on Unix?

statement: This extraction slice has no platform-name hazard checks: Windows reserved names (CON, NUL), trailing dots/spaces, case-insensitive or Unicode-normalization collisions. Case-folding collisions surface only as mid-extraction ExtractionCollision.
research_needed: Conformance corpus extracting case-colliding and reserved-name archives onto NTFS, APFS (case-insensitive) and ext4 casefold; confirm whether LogicalPath validation covers these elsewhere.
decision_needed: Must extraction preflight path collision classes for the destination platform before creating anything?

statement: SymlinkPolicy: Refuse rejects all symlinks (PolicyRefused/UnsupportedEntryKind); All accepts any target; Safe (default) rejects '/'-rooted targets, and on Windows any backslash or drive letter, and tracks '..' depth to reject lexical escape (ExtractionUnsafeSymlink).
The Safe symlink check is lexical and per link: chains can escape after extraction, e.g. p -> '.' and q -> 'p/..' both pass, but kernel resolution of q leaves the extraction root.
evidence_in_source: code inference (lexical depth counter ignores symlink components)
research_needed: Adversarial symlink-chain corpus; evaluate resolving targets against the planned extracted tree including other symlinks.
decision_needed: Must Safe policy reason about symlink-to-symlink chains, and is 'structurally impossible traversal' claimed for post-extraction consumers?

statement: Symlink creation: Unix uses symlink_contents with exact bytes; Windows always uses symlink_file (a file symlink, even for directory targets) and requires a UTF-8 target; other platforms return Unsupported.
research_needed: Test extraction of directory symlinks on Windows with and without Developer Mode/SeCreateSymbolicLinkPrivilege.
decision_needed: How are directory-versus-file symlinks and missing privileges handled on Windows?

statement: Windows security descriptor restoration is unimplemented: with Restore policy it reports 'no audited safe API in this build'; by default it reports skipped by policy.

Platform metadata restoration is unimplemented: Windows attributes, creation time, reparse original, macOS flags and birthtime are never applied, and even under Restore policy the report says restoration is unavailable.

Unix ownership restore (OwnershipPolicy::Restore) applies fchown on the open handle, refuses the u32::MAX no-change sentinel with a note, and reports failures non-fatally; with the default Ignore, recorded ownership is reported as skipped.
Unix xattr restore (XAttrPolicy::Restore) sets every recorded xattr on the file handle with no namespace filtering and reports failures; by default recorded xattrs are reported as skipped.
evidence_in_source: code; unix round-trip test (conditional on xattr support)

statement: Dangerous restoration: XAttrPolicy::Restore applies security-sensitive namespaces (security.capability grants file capabilities, security.selinux, trusted.*) with no allow-list, so a restore-enabled extraction of an untrusted archive can confer privileges.
research_needed: Threat-model xattr namespaces; compare with GNU tar --xattrs-include/exclude and bsdtar defaults.
decision_needed: Should xattr restore require an explicit namespace allow-list and exclude security/trusted by default?

statement: ACL restore (AclPolicy::Restore) re-encodes Posix1e ACLs to system.posix_acl_* xattrs on Linux, reports NFS4 ACLs as incompatible, and reports ACL restoration unavailable on other Unix platforms.

Mode restoration is not policy-gated: the recorded posix.mode (including setuid/setgid/sticky) is always applied with no umask; without posix.mode, core.executable sets 0o100 or clears all execute bits.

Dangerous restoration: the default extraction policy restores setuid/setgid/sticky bits and ignores the umask, unlike bsdtar without -p (strips SUID/SGID) and GNU tar for non-root users (applies umask).
research_needed: Verify incumbent defaults (GNU tar, bsdtar, 7-Zip, Info-ZIP) for special bits and umask; threat-model untrusted archives.
decision_needed: Should default extraction strip special mode bits and honour umask unless an explicit permissions policy is set?

statement: On non-unix destinations, recorded core.executable, posix.mode, uid/gid, xattrs and ACLs are each reported as not restorable on this platform.
File and directory mtime is restored via File::set_times (modified time only); times outside the platform SystemTime range are reported, not fatal.
Symlink metadata restoration is largely unimplemented: ownership is 'capture-only', no-follow mtime restoration is unavailable, and only xattrs are restored (Unix, Restore policy).

Symlink xattr restoration resolves destination.join(logical path) through the ambient filesystem instead of the held cap-std root, so a concurrent swap of a parent component could redirect the xattr write outside confinement.
research_needed: Race test swapping a parent directory for a symlink between symlink creation and xattr restore.

statement: Diagnostic mapping: unsupported kinds give Unsupported/UnsupportedEntryKind; collisions give PolicyRefused/ExtractionCollision; containment gives ExtractionContainmentUnavailable; all std::io errors give PolicyRefused/Io; overflow gives ResourceLimit; instability gives SourceUnstable.

Environmental I/O failures (disk full, permission denied, device errors) are classed as OutcomeClass::PolicyRefused, conflating them with deliberate policy refusal; no distinct environment or I/O outcome class exists here.
decision_needed: Should I/O failures have their own outcome class distinct from PolicyRefused?

statement: filesystem.rs unit tests: unstable_source_has_a_deterministic_bounded_failure, timestamp_round_trip_handles_both_sides_of_epoch, linux ACL round trip, windows_capture_records_bounded_attributes_and_creation_time, unix_posix_capture_and_policy_restoration_round_trip, unsafe_symlink_is_refused_before_destination_creation.

The Unix round-trip test checks only the sparse file's logical length, not recreated holes (allocated blocks), and its xattr assertions are skipped when setting the xattr fails, so sparse and xattr restoration can silently go unverified in CI.
research_needed: Assert st_blocks reduction after SparsePolicy::Restore; make xattr test failures explicit on filesystems supporting user xattrs.

statement: No test covers ACL restoration end-to-end, Windows symlink extraction, reparse refusal under KnownSafe/All, non-UTF-8 path extraction failure, or directory-mtime fidelity with symlink children.
research_needed: Add platform-matrix integration tests for each restoration policy branch.

statement: bootstrap_resource_policy ('deliberately generous limits for the experimental bootstrap CLI'): 1,000,000 entries; 64 GiB total; 16 GiB per entry; expansion ratio 64,000,000 milli; 4,000,000 chunks; path depth 1024; 1 GiB metadata; key derivation cost 0.
research_needed: Justify each default against adversarial decompression-bomb tests and real archive distributions.
decision_needed: What are the v1 default caller resource limits, given these are labelled experimental?

statement: Every bootstrap resource limit (1M entries, 64 GiB, 16 GiB, 64000x expansion, 4M chunks, depth 1024, 1 GiB metadata) is a numeric default with no cited measurement.
research_needed: Measure distributions of entry counts, sizes and expansion ratios across real archives; set limits with documented rationale.

statement: bootstrap_decode_policy: decoder window 8 MiB, working set 384 MiB (v6 permits a bounded 256 MiB JPEG/JPEG XL reconstruction working set), flags 0.
research_needed: Measure actual peak decode memory for worst-case plans versus declared 384 MiB.

statement: ExtractionPolicy defaults: collision Refuse, symlinks Safe, ownership Ignore, xattrs Ignore, sparse Logical, acls Ignore, windows_security Ignore, reparse Refuse, platform_metadata Ignore, with bootstrap budget and decode limits; policy is caller-constructed, never archive-controlled.

Platform access in this slice depends on cap-std (range '4.0.3', not exact-pinned unlike most dependencies), rustix =1.1.4 and xattr =1.6.1 (Unix only). The workspace forbids unsafe_code, which motivates the 'no audited safe API' refusals.
research_needed: Audit cap-std/rustix/xattr maintenance and security history; decide pinning policy for the confinement-critical crate.
decision_needed: Should cap-std be exact-pinned like other dependencies, and is a vetted unsafe FFI crate admissible for Windows/macOS metadata?

statement: Frozen report format identifiers: inspection JSON is 'entrybound/inspection-v1' and diff JSON is 'entrybound/archive-diff-v1', each emitting "version":1.
research_needed: Publish JSON schemas and a stability policy for these report formats.

statement: Repack options: RepackMode is RepresentationOnly or Replan(CompressionProfile); IndexPolicy is Preserve, Present or Absent; RepackOptions combines mode, target Layout, index policy and StreamWindow.

RepackAnalysis reports source/target layout, planner, chunk references, unique chunks, stored chunk bytes, decode working set, dictionary/group/region counts, PCRs, output bytes and LAI/AUX/PCR equality flags.

prepare_repack encodes and fully re-opens the output in memory without touching the filesystem, returning PreparedRepack (encoded, verified, analysis) 'ready for staged publication'; publication is the caller's job (CLI entrybound-cli/src/lib.rs:3395).

Encrypted repack is refused: a source with FEATURE_ENCRYPTED_INDEXED_V1 (0x20) returns Unsupported/CryptoLayoutUnsupported, 'encrypted repack is deferred; decrypting to an unencrypted output is never implicit'.

Encrypted repack is explicitly deferred. The key requirements (same recipients, re-encryption epoch, password re-entry) and any explicit decrypt-to-plain conversion path are unspecified in this slice.
decision_needed: How should encrypted repack work (re-encrypt under same recipient set, require unlock, explicit --decrypt flag), and is it v1 scope?

statement: A STREAM target with IndexPolicy Present or Absent is rejected as Nonconforming/CommandUsage ('STREAM has no Index').

RepresentationOnly repack clones the source EAM (plans, dictionaries and groups retained); Replan calls replan_archive. Preserve includes an Index if the source was STREAM or its Index was not RebuiltAbsent, so a source with an invalid Index gains a fresh valid one.

An INDEXED target clears FEATURE_STREAM_LAYOUT_V1, zeroes stream_dedup_window, then encodes and runs open(). A STREAM target encodes with the chosen window and reopens via open_stream_with_limits (bootstrap limits, Retain); budget_declared is false only for representation-only repack of an undeclared-budget STREAM source.

Post-write repack identity invariant: output LAI and AUX must equal the source in every mode, and PCR must also be equal for RepresentationOnly; violation yields Corrupt with LaiMismatch, AuxMismatch or PcrMismatch.

Repack is fully in memory: the source archive, the target EAM and output bytes are all held, and STREAM output is cloned again for verification. Bounded-memory repack of archives larger than RAM is not implemented.

Repack physical metrics: chunk count is total ContentObject chunk references, unique is distinct chunks, and stored bytes is the sum of Index stored_len (excluding manifest, dictionary, reconstruction data and section/frame overhead).
prepare_repack does not handle SignatureSet, embedded signatures, timestamps or other physical-scope bindings; whether repack strips, invalidates, re-binds or refuses signed inputs is unaddressed.
research_needed: Test repack of a signed unencrypted archive (if supported) and report signature status on the output.
decision_needed: What happens to physical-scope and logical-scope signatures on repack?

statement: Diff model: DiffTier SEMANTIC/AUXILIARY/PHYSICAL/CONTAINER; DiffIdentityStatus SAME/DIFFERENT/NOT_VERIFIED/NOT_COMPUTED; DiffChange (tier, subject, field, left, right) sorted by derived Ord; ArchiveDiffReport with per-root statuses, interpretation, scopes, optional PhysicalDiffSummary.
Diff JSON is a hand-written fixed-order serializer (no serde) that escapes quote, backslash, \n, \r, \t and other control characters as \u00XX, ending in a newline.
ArchiveDiffReport::to_canonical_json is not exercised by any unit or integration test, so its canonical, stable output is unverified.
research_needed: Golden-file tests for diff JSON across releases.

statement: archive_diff compares two fully verified OpenedArchives. It computes semantic, auxiliary, physical and container changes and root equality, then picks an interpretation ladder string ('semantic content differs' ... 'exact verified container identity is equal') and a physical summary.
Diff pairs entries only by exact logical path string. Renames and moves show as a removal plus an addition, with no rename detection or content-move matching.
Semantic diff fields: entry presence, kind, identity-participating metadata, content_digest, logical_size, symlink_target (length and SHA-256 only), and windows_reparse_point (tag, length, SHA-256).
Metadata diffs are tiered by participates_in_identity_v1, true only for core.executable. mtime, POSIX mode, uid/gid, xattrs, ACLs, hardlink group and platform metadata are AUXILIARY.

Under identity-v1, security-relevant changes (POSIX mode 0644 to 0600, ACL grants, ownership) change only AUX, never LAI; whether signatures and 'same archive' claims must cover permissions depends on AUX binding.
research_needed: Trace which roots each signature scope binds; threat-model permission tampering that preserves LAI.
decision_needed: Is excluding mode/ownership/ACLs from LAI acceptable for signed-archive semantics, or is an identity profile covering them needed?

statement: Auxiliary diff covers FidelityReport inequality (captured/unavailable/degraded counts), conversion provenance (source digest) and legacy preservation (source digest).

Physical diff covers planner_id, chunker_id, chunk digest set, physical order, transform plans, dictionaries, chunk groups, reconstruction data/regions/fallbacks/audits (counts only) and per-ContentObject chunk sequences.
PhysicalDiffSummary counts chunks reused, added and removed by chunk-digest set, plus ContentObjects present on both sides whose chunk boundaries changed.
research_needed: Use for measuring CDC resynchronization and incremental-update reuse on version-series corpora.

statement: Container diff covers PCI, layout, index_status and the full FeatureSet; when features differ, only incompat bits are printed as values (read_only_compat and compat are omitted).

archive_metadata_diff compares range-backed RandomAccessMetadata. LAI/AUX count as equal only when both sides are Verified, otherwise NOT_VERIFIED; PCR is always NOT_VERIFIED and PCI NOT_COMPUTED. Scopes report bytes fetched and range requests.

The metadata-only diff omits logical_size changes, auxiliary evidence (fidelity, conversion, preservation), chunk-set and physical summary, and index status, so remote diff is less complete than local diff.
archive_metadata_diff and random_inspection_json have no unit or integration tests, and entrybound-cli tests (cli_workflow.rs, crypto_cli.rs) contain no repack or diff command cases.
research_needed: Add HTTP-range fixtures (tests/random_access.rs style) for metadata diff and random inspection, and CLI repack/diff tests.

statement: For partial verification the metadata-diff interpretation collapses mixed states (LAI NOT_VERIFIED with AUX different, or LAI same with AUX unverified) into the generic 'metadata compared; unread physical/container bytes remain unverified'.
decision_needed: What user-facing interpretation is required for each partial-verification combination?

statement: kind_name covers exactly directory, file, symlink and reparse-point, confirming a four-variant EntryKind with no FIFO, socket or device kinds.
Index status labels: present-valid, rebuilt-absent, rebuilt-invalid, not-applicable-stream.

Diff/explain value text: timestamps 'seconds.nanoseconds' (precision and restorable omitted, so precision-only differences print identical sides); xattrs name:len:sha256; sparse maps size/extents/sha256; ACLs as counts; security descriptors and reparse data as length/sha256.
InspectionViews selectors are entries, plans, chunks, reconstruction, provenance, security and access; selecting none yields all views.

InspectionSecurity carries crypto-layer context for reporting only (encrypted, payload suite, recipient-set digest, archive_id, embedded signature counts: valid, invalid, unsupported, stale) and never participates in EAM interpretation.

Inspection JSON header: namespace, format major/minor, layout, role (literal "Complete"), incompat/read-only-compat/compat features, the four identity roots with status VERIFIED, declared resource budget, and decode requirements.

inspection_json unconditionally prints 'whole archive verified', status VERIFIED and role Complete, trusting the caller to pass a fully verified OpenedArchive; the type does not encode verification scope or role.
decision_needed: Should verification state be carried in the OpenedArchive type so reports cannot overstate scope?

statement: The entries view prints path, kind, content object, logical bytes, symlink target encoding/length/SHA-256 (not target text), mtime details, POSIX mode/uid/gid/hardlink group/sparse summary, xattrs as name hex/length/SHA-256 (values withheld), ACL counts, and Windows/macOS summaries.
The plans view prints plan id, identifier, codec, codec parameters in hex, transform steps, dictionary reference, window bytes, working-set bytes and decode flags.

The chunks view prints unique chunks, logical references, unique plaintext bytes, deduplicated bytes and min/avg/max chunk size, plus per-chunk records in physical order (digest, ordinal, logical bytes, plan id, group, stored bytes).

The reconstruction view prints reconstruction data object count/bytes, region and JPEG-region counts, worst access chunks/bytes, per-region records with access costs, and reconstruction audits (target, transform, reason).
The provenance view prints conversion source format, source digest and import mode (or nulls), FidelityReport unavailable and degraded counts, and whether legacy preservation evidence is present.
The security view asserts rather than computes two fields: private_metadata_authenticated is set equal to 'encrypted', and secret_material_exposed is hardcoded false.
research_needed: Derive both fields from authenticated crypto state; test with public-metadata encrypted variants if any exist.

statement: The access view prints random_entry_lookup, stream_dedup_window, index status, chunk group count, maximum lookback and worst group random-access bytes.

random_inspection_json emits reduced range-backed inspection with 'whole_archive_verified=false'. Per-root statuses are VERIFIED, NOT_REQUESTED, DECLARED_NOT_FULLY_VERIFIED or NOT_COMPUTED; PCI is null. It adds entry/object counts, planner/chunker IDs, source_revision_stable, section count, bytes fetched and range requests.

Explanation evidence classes are RECORDED (persisted in archive), DERIVED (computed from recorded facts), AUDIT (persisted reconstruction audits) and NOT_RECORDED; facts carry subject, field and value strings.

Archive-level explain facts: planner and chunker IDs; logical and stored chunk bytes; physical_savings_bytes (unique plaintext minus stored chunk bytes, may be negative, ignores dedup and container overhead); unique chunks; references; dictionary/group/region counts; per-plan codec, identifier and working set.

Planner decision evidence is not persisted: explain always reports unselected_candidate_comparisons as NOT_RECORDED ('not persisted by this archive'), so explanations cannot cite rejected codec, chunking or lookback alternatives or their costs.
research_needed: Estimate size cost of persisting a compact planner audit trail; usability value of 'why' explanations.
decision_needed: Should the planner persist candidate comparisons (in-archive or sidecar) for explainability?

statement: Entry explain looks up the path linearly (absent gives PolicyRefused/RandomAccessEntryNotFound) and records kind, every metadata item, a coarse restorability ('policy- and platform-dependent' or 'bootstrap metadata only'), and symlink or reparse facts.

Explain says reparse restorability is 'refused by default; exact restoration requires Windows and an explicit policy', but materialize refuses reparse entries under every ReparsePolicy including All, so the explanation overstates what the implementation can do.
research_needed: Align explain text with actual ReparsePolicy behaviour; add a test.

statement: File explain facts: content object, chunk count, logical bytes, per-chunk codec and plan, dedup-shared chunks, dictionary dependencies, lookback predecessors, reconstruction regions, worst reconstruction bytes, dependency closure bytes, max decode working set, and estimated_range_count.

Explain's lookback set is one level (same-group chunks within max_lookback positions before each requested chunk), while random-access decoding recursively decodes prerequisites, so dependency_closure_logical_bytes and estimated_range_count may underestimate real access cost.
research_needed: Compare explain estimates with measured fetch counts and bytes from tests/random_access.rs::random_access_fetches_dictionary_and_bounded_lookback_dependencies on Dense/Extreme archives.
decision_needed: Is the ChunkGroup dependency closure transitive by specification, and must explain report the transitive closure?

statement: estimated_range_count is a heuristic sum (requested chunks + dictionaries + extra lookback predecessors + regions). It ignores metadata sections, Index and descriptor fetches, range coalescing and region-internal chunks, and is not validated against HTTP measurements.
research_needed: Validate against RandomAccessVerificationReport.range_request_count on representative archives.

statement: Persisted reconstruction audits appear as AUDIT-class 'reconstruction_fallback' facts naming transform ID and reason.

Tooling indexes model maps directly (transform_plans[index], chunks[digest], plans[&plan_ref], chunk_groups[&group]) and would panic on an inconsistent model; it relies on prior EAM validation of the OpenedArchive.
research_needed: Fuzz inspection/explain with validated edge-case archives to confirm no panic paths.

statement: tooling.rs unit tests: representation_repack_preserves_all_native_roots, replanning_preserves_semantic_and_auxiliary_roots, diff_places_index_only_change_in_container_tier, diff_keeps_conversion_evidence_in_auxiliary_tier, hardlink_topology_is_auxiliary_not_semantic_or_physical, platform_security_diff_respects_auxiliary_and_semantic_tiers, structured_json_and_evidence_classes_are_stable.

Tested diff behaviour: an Index-only difference is CONTAINER-tier with equal LAI/AUX/PCR; a changed conversion source digest is AUXILIARY; hardlink topology is AUXILIARY with equal PCR; an ACL change is AUXILIARY; File to ReparsePoint is a SEMANTIC kind change with different LAI.
Tested replan: Fast to Dense keeps LAI and AUX, changes PCR, sets target planner 'dense-v6' and, with Index Absent, yields RebuiltAbsent; the diff shows no SEMANTIC or AUXILIARY changes.

Untested repack and explain paths: encrypted-source refusal, STREAM plus index usage error, Replan to the same profile (would expose the chunker_id PCR divergence), inspection view subsets, explain on dictionary or lookback archives, and budget_declared propagation.
research_needed: Add targeted tests per branch; include a Replan(same profile) PCR stability test.

statement: The inspection stability test only checks that two calls in one process give byte-identical output and contain the format ID; there are no golden files, schema checks, or cross-version stability tests for the 'stable' JSON.
research_needed: Golden JSON fixtures versioned with the report format IDs.
